clauses.clause: Use a variety of communication modes to share information (C)

verdicts.evidence: 'I think Papa is __________ because ________________________.' ... Tell students that they may begin writing their responses to Part II.
verdicts.rationale: Students share relevant and accurate information about the story's characters and setting through written responses on the Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me response sheet (Parts I and II): "Tell students that they may begin writing their responses to Part I" (characters and setting) and Part II using the sentence frame "I think Papa is __________ because ________________________." Students also share orally during Turn and Talks and the Pinky Partners protocol ("What do you imagine when you look up at the night sky?"). However, the "variety of different modes" clause is not fully met: while students do use oral sharing (Turn and Talk, Pinky Partners) and written responses, the lesson does not intentionally set out to have students share information through a deliberate variety of communication modes (e.g., digital, visual presentation, etc.) as the standard's construction purpose requires. The oral sharing moments are primarily comprehension discussions rather than constructed sharing of researched/accurate information through varied modes. The written response is the only substantive (C) sharing act, capping the variety-of-modes clause at not met.

However, the student is choosing from a pre-supplied word bank and completing a scaffolded sentence frame rather than independently crafting an engaging text — the descriptive-word use is real but narrow and frame-bound, and the product is a single-sentence response rather than a crafted, engaging text.

verdicts.evidence: 'I think Papa is __________ because ________________________.' Remind students that in the first blank they will write the descriptive word they circled above. In the second blank they will write why they think Papa is best described that way.
verdicts.rationale: The standard requires students to use descriptive words to craft engaging texts (a Construction act). In Work Time C, Part II, students select a descriptive word from a word bank (tired, sneaky, scared, kind) and complete the sentence frame "I think Papa is __________ because __________," writing a descriptive word and a reason. This is a genuine (C) act — the student writes using a descriptive word. However, the descriptive-word use is constrained to a single pre-supplied adjective placed into a scaffolded frame, and the resulting product is a one-sentence response sheet answer rather than a crafted, engaging text. The narrow scope of descriptive-word deployment and the frame-bound nature of the writing cap this at partially met.
